summary: This is a fresh run (0 nodes) on the ESCI v2 dense-retrieval task with the rubert-tiny-lite SentenceTransformer backbone. There is no in-run baseline yet, so the first job is to land a clean, working single-GPU recipe and then climb from the known ~0.88 plateau. The prior sibling landscape is decisive: (a) rubert-dr-0807 #9 reached recall@100=0.8776 with a clean symmetric in-batch InfoNCE recipe (bs 8192, accumulate 2, lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, grad_clip 1.0, temp 0.05, OneCycleLR pct_start 0.2, 10 epochs, positive_threshold=1), and the documented 67-node plateau is 0.8835 with DCL(nll_cos)+R-Drop (alpha 0.5, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, OneCycleLR max_lr 1e-3, AdamW wd 0.01 no-decay, ~32k effective batch, 50-60 epochs); (b) hard-negative mining is the proven escape from that plateau (+0.03-0.04 on e5-small, never ported to this tiny backbone), and the unified repo already implements qwen3 (hard-neg cross-batch InfoNCE) + NegativesCollator + nll_cos; (c) many sibling attempts failed on infra (DDP group-size, collator API mismatch, unused-parameters, missing looplab_eval.py, subprocess in test.py) rather than on method. The strongest untried, highest-ceiling levers on this backbone are therefore: (1) externally/teacher-mined hard negatives with positive-aware false-negative filtering fed into nll_cos (the #1 proven lever, never landed on rubert-tiny-lite), (2) faithful DCL+R-Drop reproduction with the exact OneCycleLR/AdamW recipe and long horizon, and (3) listwise-KL distillation from a stronger frozen teacher (bge@0.902). Every node must declare {"gpus":1}, use single-GPU code (no multi-GPU DDP paths that crashed siblings), and print RECALL@100 to stdout.
reasoning:
I approached this as a fresh-run review with no in-run experiments, so the value is entirely in (a) extracting the accumulated prior knowledge from sibling runs and the distilled benchmark note, and (b) mapping it onto concrete first experiments that avoid the failure modes that killed prior attempts.

Evidence gathering: I read the benchmark note (esci-dense-retrieval-rubert-tiny-lite-v1-v2-benc-7690ad0a.md) which distills the key recipe and levers. I read sibling runs: rubertlite-dense-retrieval (#0=0.8077 baseline, #1 failed loss-stagnant), rubertlite-dr-unified-v2 (all 3 crashed on collator API / subprocess / DDP; #4 landed 0.225), rubertlite-dr-unified-v6 (mnr 0.7088, symmetric mnsr 0.7151, nll_cos 0.728, merges 0.7281/0.225), rubertlite-dr-unified-v7 (R-Drop nodes pending/superseded; label-smoothing, multi-positive, DCL-threshold all superseded by freshness gate; #0/#1 R-Drop pending), and rubert-dr-0807 (the richest: #9=0.8776 clean InfoNCE anchor, #7=0.8173 FN-mask at degenerate temp 0.01, #11 temp sweep 0.852, #12/#13 merges 0.8668/0.8651, plus many crashes on DDP group-size, unused-parameters, missing looplab_eval.py, validation gather). I also consulted cross-run memory/lessons (nll_cos supported; merging symmetric InfoNCE into DCL negligible; hard-negative mining supported) and grounded techniques with web/arXiv sources (R-Drop 2106.14448, ESCI 2206.06588, amazon-science/esci-data repo).

Key synthesis: The plateau is ~0.8835 (DCL+R-Drop). The documented +0.03-0.04 escape is hard-negative mining, which was measured on e5-small but never successfully ported to rubert-tiny-lite in these runs (every attempt crashed on infra). So the single highest-value first experiment is a clean, single-GPU hard-negative + nll_cos run that actually completes. The second is a faithful DCL+R-Drop reproduction with the exact optimizer/scheduler recipe (the unified-repo runs used repo-default cosine/AdamW wd 0.1, confounding the batch-size comparison; the winning recipe used OneCycleLR + AdamW wd 0.01 no-decay). The third is distillation from a stronger teacher, which is completely unexplored.

I deliberately did not cite the wrong arXiv ID I first guessed (2104.14448, a math paper) — I only cite the fetched R-Drop page (2106.14448). All claims cite the nodes/runs I actually read and the URLs I actually fetched.
findings: No in-run experiments exist yet (0 nodes); the run needs a first clean baseline before any method comparison.

The strongest verified anchor in the portfolio is rubert-dr-0807 #9: recall@100=0.8776 with clean symmetric in-batch InfoNCE (bs 8192, accumulate 2, lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, grad_clip 1.0, temp 0.05, OneCycleLR pct_start 0.2, 10 epochs, positive_threshold=1).

The documented rubert-tiny-lite plateau is 0.8835 via DCL(nll_cos)+R-Drop (alpha 0.5, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, OneCycleLR max_lr 1e-3, AdamW wd 0.01 with no-decay on bias/LayerNorm/word_embeddings, ~32k effective batch, 50-60 epochs).

Hard-negative mining is the proven escape from the plateau (+0.03-0.04 recall@100 measured on e5-small with NV-Embed/cosine-threshold 0.264 mined negatives), but was never successfully ported to rubert-tiny-lite — every attempt crashed on infra.
The unified repo already implements the needed machinery: qwen3 loss (hard-neg cross-batch InfoNCE), NegativesCollator, and nll_cos (DCL port) — the blocker is wiring it without DDP crashes.

A recurring failure mode across siblings is multi-GPU/DDP infra: torch distributed _get_group_size crashes (rubert-dr-0807 #8/#10), unused-parameters in LightningModule (#0), collator API mismatch preprocess_fn vs tokenize_fn (unified-v2 #0/#1/#2), missing looplab_eval.py (#2), and subprocess.run inside test.py (#2). Single-GPU code avoids all of these.
FN-masking tested at degenerate temp=0.01 regressed (0.8173); the recipe must keep temp in the healthy 0.02-0.1 range (temp sweep #11 peaked 0.852 at the anchor recipe).

The unified-repo DCL runs used the repo-default cosine/AdamW wd 0.1, which confounds the batch-size comparison against the documented OneCycleLR/wd-0.01 recipe — the exact optimizer/scheduler recipe was never faithfully reproduced in the unified repo.
Distillation from a stronger frozen teacher (bge@0.902) is completely unexplored in these runs and is a high-ceiling supervision lever given the plateau.
ESCI labels are all 1 (positive_threshold must be 1, not default 2, or zero positives crash); the data is multilingual (EN/JA/ES) with up to 40 judged results per query.

claims.statement: A clean symmetric in-batch InfoNCE recipe reached recall@100=0.8776 on rubert-tiny-lite (bs 8192, accumulate 2, lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, temp 0.05, OneCycleLR pct_start 0.2, 10 epochs, positive_threshold=1).

The documented rubert-tiny-lite plateau is recall@100=0.8835 with DCL(nll_cos)+R-Drop (alpha 0.5, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, AdamW wd 0.01 no-decay, OneCycleLR max_lr 1e-3, ~32k effective batch, 50-60 epochs).

Hard-negative mining is the proven escape from the ~0.8835 plateau (+0.03-0.04 recall@100 on e5-small with NV-Embed/cosine-threshold 0.264 mined negatives), never successfully ported to rubert-tiny-lite.

Sibling attempts on this task repeatedly failed on multi-GPU/DDP and collator infra (torch distributed group-size crash, LightningModule unused-parameters, preprocess_fn vs tokenize_fn collator API mismatch, missing looplab_eval.py, subprocess.run in test.py), not on method.
FN-masking evaluated at degenerate temperature 0.01 regressed to 0.8173; the temperature sweep at the healthy anchor recipe peaked at 0.852, indicating temperature must stay in the 0.02-0.1 range.
The unified-repo DCL(nll_cos) runs used the repo-default cosine/AdamW wd 0.1 recipe (0.728), so the documented OneCycleLR/wd-0.01 recipe was never faithfully reproduced in the unified repo.
R-Drop regularizes dropout by minimizing bidirectional KL between two dropout-sampled output distributions and is effective when fine-tuning large pre-trained models (NeurIPS 2021).
The ESCI Shopping Queries Dataset is a multilingual (EN/JA/ES) benchmark of ~130k queries and 2.6M labeled (query,product) judgements with up to 40 judged results per query.

recommended_directions: EXPERIMENT 1 (land the baseline + prove the #1 lever): Single-GPU hard-negative-mined nll_cos run on the unified repo. Use loss= nll_cos (DCL port) with the proven numeric recipe (bs 8192, accumulate 2, lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, grad_clip 1.0, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, warmup 0.2, ~10-20 epochs), enable train.negatives vector mining with cosine-threshold ~0.264 or a frozen teacher (NV-Embed/bge) to supply 1-2 hard negatives per query, and apply positive-aware false-negative filtering (fn_mask_ratio ~0.95) so near-duplicate true positives are not treated as negatives. Declare {"gpus":1}, single-GPU only, print RECALL@100. This directly targets the +0.03-0.04 escape that has never landed on this backbone.

EXPERIMENT 2 (faithful DCL+R-Drop reproduction): Port the exact documented 0.8835 recipe into the unified repo: nll_cos with rdrop_alpha=0.5, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, uniformity_weight 0, batch-centering off, AdamW wd 0.01 with no-decay on bias/LayerNorm/word_embeddings, OneCycleLR max_lr 1e-3 pct_start 0.2 div_factor 25 anneal-cos cycle_momentum off, effective batch ~32k (bs 16384 accumulate 2 on one GPU), grad_clip 1.0, fp16, 50-60 epochs, positive_threshold 1. This resolves the confound in the unified-repo DCL runs and establishes the true in-run ceiling before adding mining.

EXPERIMENT 3 (distillation, highest ceiling, unexplored): Listwise-KL distillation of retrieval score distributions from a frozen stronger teacher (e.g. bge@0.902) into rubert-tiny-lite, aligning softmax-over-candidates between student and teacher at kd_temperature ~0.05, kd_weight ~1.0, optionally combined with the nll_cos contrastive term. This is the only completely unexplored supervision lever and directly attacks the plateau.

EXPERIMENT 4 (cheap robustness sweep once a working anchor exists): On the EXPERIMENT 1 anchor, sweep temperature {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} and rdrop_alpha {0, 0.5} at fixed effective batch to confirm the healthy operating range before scaling epochs — mirrors the finding that temp 0.01 is degenerate.

verdicts.statement: A clean symmetric in-batch InfoNCE recipe reached recall@100=0.8776 on rubert-tiny-lite (bs 8192, accumulate 2, lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, temp 0.05, OneCycleLR pct_start 0.2, 10 epochs, positive_threshold=1).

The documented rubert-tiny-lite plateau is recall@100=0.8835 with DCL(nll_cos)+R-Drop (alpha 0.5, temp 0.05, thr 0.1, AdamW wd 0.01 no-decay, OneCycleLR max_lr 1e-3, ~32k effective batch, 50-60 epochs).

Hard-negative mining is the proven escape from the ~0.8835 plateau (+0.03-0.04 recall@100 on e5-small with NV-Embed/cosine-threshold 0.264 mined negatives), never successfully ported to rubert-tiny-lite.

Sibling attempts on this task repeatedly failed on multi-GPU/DDP and collator infra (torch distributed group-size crash, LightningModule unused-parameters, preprocess_fn vs tokenize_fn collator API mismatch, missing looplab_eval.py, subprocess.run in test.py), not on method.
FN-masking evaluated at degenerate temperature 0.01 regressed to 0.8173; the temperature sweep at the healthy anchor recipe peaked at 0.852, indicating temperature must stay in the 0.02-0.1 range.
The unified-repo DCL(nll_cos) runs used the repo-default cosine/AdamW wd 0.1 recipe (0.728), so the documented OneCycleLR/wd-0.01 recipe was never faithfully reproduced in the unified repo.
R-Drop regularizes dropout by minimizing bidirectional KL between two dropout-sampled output distributions and is effective when fine-tuning large pre-trained models (NeurIPS 2021).
